text.p: Dutch-Belgian financial group Fortis said on Wednesday its parent companies expected higher Fortis group earnings per share (EPS) in 1997.

"The organic development of the Fortis companies, and the immediate positive contribution of MeesPierson, to the profit of Fortis are expected to produce ongoing profit growth in 1997, barring unforseen circumstances," Fortis said.
"On the basis of this outlook for Fortis, both parent companies expect another increase in earnings per share for 1997," the company said.

Fortis, a banking and insurance group equally owned by Fortis Amev of the Netherlands and Belgium's Fortis AG, earlier announced a net profit of 731 million ECUs compared with 631 million ECUs in 1995.
Fortis bought investment bank MeesPierson from Dutch bank ABN AMRO last year for 2.5 billion guilders.
Fortis Amev's EPS rose to 4.42 guilders from 3.85 guilders, while Fortis AG's EPS increased to 355 Belgian francs from 310 francs.
